narrative: The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 39.0%. Although that is below half, it was above the stricter risk cutoff used for this loan, so your application was denied. The most influential factor was your checking-account status: no checking account was recorded. This is common among approved applicants and actually counted in your favour. The next most important factor was the loan purpose. You requested credit for a new car, a purpose that is less common among approved applicants and pushed the assessment toward higher risk. The third factor was the presence of a co-applicant. Only a small share of approved applicants had another debtor or guarantor listed, and this also pushed toward bad credit. These risk-raising factors, together with other less influential details, outweighed the positive signal from your checking-account status. Your requested amount of 1,287 DM is well below the approved average of about 3,020 DM, and your 10-month term is shorter than the average 19 months, but those strengths were not enough to offset the main concerns. Next, ask the lender for a manual review and for the specific cutoff that applied. Provide proof of stable income and employment, clarify the car purchase, and ask whether adding savings information or changing the co-applicant arrangement would allow a revised application.
